summary: Cybershore PrivateLink: auth retry-thrash causing tenant autoscaler oscillation, streaming resets, and billing spike
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-01 11:18 UTC Cybershore reported widespread streaming resets and large increases in per-tenant token billing for their private deployment. Initial symptoms: burst of 5xx and cancelled streams from client side, followed by a rapid series of new connections from the same tenant that correlated with backend auth failures. Impact: degraded throughput for Cybershore's customer-facing chat tier (~40% error rate at peak), elevated costs due to repeated model cold-starts and failed completions, and customer SLA exposure.

Impact:
- Customer streaming sessions truncated and retried, causing duplicate partial responses and billing anomalies.
- Autoscaler for the tenant oscillated (scale-up then immediate eviction) causing GPU churn and cold-cache penalties.
- Several retries were routed to fallback larger model variants, increasing cost.

Environment details:
- Private deployment (VPC peering + PrivateLink) in us-east-1.
- Control plane on private cluster (v2.8.3).
- Auth service (token validation) running version 1.14.
- Customer uses client library with aggressive keepalive and immediate reconnect on stream terminate.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Using a PrivateLink-configured tenant, configure the client SDK with keepalive interval 10s and immediate reconnect on error.
2) Force the control plane auth service to return transient 503s (simulated in staging via fault injection).
3) Observe repeated reconnects, auth failures, and autoscaler activity.

timeline: 2026-03-01T11:18 UTC - Cybershore reported customer-impacting streaming resets via support channel (#support-private).
2026-03-01T11:25 UTC - On-call SRE (Sanjay) triaged, identified auth-service transient errors and correlation with client reconnects.
2026-03-01T11:40 UTC - Escalated to Platform Engineering; incident declared (INC-20260301-01).

2026-03-01T12:05 UTC - Implemented emergency mitigation: disabled aggressive immediate reconnect policy server-side (introduce 2s jitter, exponential backoff at proxy), and applied temporary token-validation cache backstop for authenticated sessions.
2026-03-01T12:30 UTC - Streaming error rate for Cybershore dropped from 40% to <5%.
2026-03-01T13:00 UTC - Hotfix PR merged: add auth retry budget and exponential backoff enforcement at proxy (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821).
2026-03-01T13:45 UTC - Hotfix rolled to prod private control plane for affected region; customer confirmed restoration of normal traffic patterns.
2026-03-03T09:00 UTC - Post-incident review scheduled with Cybershore and internal stakeholders; action items assigned.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Control plane auth-service transient upstream latency caused token validation failures; client SDK's immediate reconnect behavior amplified load and triggered autoscaler scaling loops.
Hypothesis 2: Token validation has low caching TTL for PrivateLink tenants, so every reconnect forced an auth-path call causing thundering herd when many clients reconnect simultaneously.

Finding: Auth-service introduced a regression in 1.14 where a dependent upstream (internal cert verification service) had reduced concurrency under load leading to 503s; combined with client reconnect patterns this produced the observed oscillation.

Telemetry: Traces show auth validation latency tail rising to >2s during peak, median 40ms. Autoscaler reacted to CPU/Queue length signals within 6s, scaling up and causing cold-cache penalties visible in serving-runtime metrics.
customer_communication: 2026-03-01T11:30 UTC - Acknowledged receipt; informed customer we are triaging and provided initial ETA 60 minutes. (Leah)

2026-03-01T12:10 UTC - Informed customer of temporary mitigation (backoff/jitter) and expected reduction in retries; requested that they hold off client-side SDK updates until stability confirmed. (Sanjay)
2026-03-01T13:50 UTC - Notified customer that hotfix is deployed and asked to validate traffic. Customer reported downstream errors resolved and provided sample logs. (Leah)
2026-03-03T09:30 UTC - Sent post-incident brief with root cause, mitigations, billing remediation plan, and next steps. (Leah)
Customer response: Appreciative of fast mitigation; requested credit for duplicated token charges during incident window and asked for long-term solution timeline.
resolution:
Root cause: a concurrency regression in cert-verification upstream of auth-service (introduced in 1.14) caused intermittent 503s. This combined with customer SDK's immediate reconnect semantics and low token-cache TTL produced a feed-forward reconnect-amplification loop that triggered tenant autoscaler oscillation and cold-start billing spikes.

Fixes applied:
- Emergency server-side mitigation: enforce server-side reconnect backoff + 2s jitter to prevent reconnect storms.
- Hotfix to auth-service: increase upstream concurrency limits and fail faster with clearer retryable error classification (PR merged and deployed).
- Added token-validation backstop cache for PrivateLink tenants to allow 30s cache during auth upstream errors.
- Billing remediation: finance to issue credit for duplicate charges during incident window (see linked internal billing ticket INT-44012).

Status: Hotfix deployed 2026-03-01 13:45 UTC, customer traffic stabilized. Monitoring retention 72h; no regressions observed as of 2026-03-03.
postincident_actions: Action 1: Platform - revert auth-service regression in next patch release and add capacity tests for upstream cert-verifier (owner: Platform Eng, due 2026-03-10).
Action 2: Developer Experience - update Private SDK default reconnect policy to include exponential backoff and jitter; publish patch to SDK (owner: DevX, due 2026-03-12).
Action 3: SRE - add tenant-level autoscaler damping factor for private tenants to avoid rapid oscillation under short auth blips (owner: SRE, due 2026-03-08).
Action 4: Billing - review affected invoices and issue customer credit; coordinate with CS and Finance (owner: Billing Ops, due 2026-03-05, linked INT-44012).
Action 5: Docs - publish post-incident runbook outlining PrivateLink auth failure mitigation patterns and recommended SDK settings for private customers (owner: Solutions Eng, due 2026-03-09).
